topic: Fundamentals of Vectors: The Language of Space
target_audience: High school students or beginners in STEM

outline.topic: Fundamentals of Vectors: The Language of Space
outline.target_audience: High school students or beginners in STEM

sections.title: What is a Vector? (Intuitive Concept)
sections.content: Define vectors as entities possessing both magnitude (length) and direction. Contrast with 'scalars' (magnitude only) using a visual arrow representation on a 2D coordinate plane.
sections.example: A squirrel running 5 meters (magnitude) North-East (direction) from its tree.

sections.title: Visualizing Vector Addition
sections.content: Introduce the 'Tip-to-Tail' method. Explain how connecting the end of one vector to the start of another creates a resultant vector, emphasizing that order does not change the result (Commutative Property).
sections.example: A drone flies 3 units right, then 4 units up; the resultant vector is the direct diagonal path from start to finish.

sections.title: The Components of a Vector
sections.content: Break down vectors into 'x' and 'y' components (Basis vectors i and j). Use a grid system to show how any vector can be expressed as a linear combination of these basis units.
sections.example: Representing a character's velocity in a game: v = 3i + 2j, where 3 is the horizontal speed and 2 is the vertical jump speed.

sections.title: Scaling Vectors (Scalar Multiplication)
sections.content: Explain how multiplying a vector by a scalar changes its magnitude without altering its direction (unless the scalar is negative). Use animation to show the arrow stretching or shrinking.
sections.example: A robotic arm extending its reach: multiplying the 'direction' vector by 2 to make it twice as long.

sections.title: Summary & Real-World Application
sections.content: Recap: Vectors represent movement and physical properties. Close with a summary of how these concepts form the bedrock of physics engines in games and coordinate navigation.
sections.example: Using vectors to calculate the trajectory of an angry bird aimed at a target structure.

storyboard.title: What is a Vector? (Intuitive Concept)
lecture_lines: Vectors act like arrows in space.
animations: Display an arrow on screen. Color: #FFFFFF. Label: 'Vector v'.
Show the arrow moving from the origin. Color: #FF00FF. Label: 'Vector v'.
Display a second identical vector alongside. Color: #00FFFF. Label: 'Vector u'.

storyboard.title: Visualizing Vector Addition
lecture_lines: The resultant connects start to finish.
animations: Show vectors u and v head-to-tail. Color: #00FFFF, #FF00FF. Label: 'u', 'v'.
Draw the resultant vector from origin. Color: #FFFF00. Label: 'u + v'.
Animate vector u sliding to connect to vector v. Color: #00FFFF. Label: 'u + v'.

storyboard.title: The Components of a Vector
lecture_lines: Break vectors into x and y.
Use i and j basis units.
animations: Draw grid lines on background. Color: #333333.
Place vector v onto the grid. Color: #FFFFFF. Label: 'Vector v'.
Project vector v onto X and Y axes. Color: #FF0000, #00FF00. Labels: 'vx', 'vy'.

storyboard.title: Scaling Vectors (Scalar Multiplication)
animations: Display vector v. Color: #FFFFFF. Label: 'Vector v'.
Animate stretching vector v by 2. Color: #00FF00. Label: '2v'.
Animate shrinking vector v by 0.5. Color: #FF0000. Label: '0.5v'.

storyboard.title: Summary & Real-World Application
animations: Display a collection of vectors together. Color: #FFFFFF. Labels: 'Set of Vectors'.
Highlight a single vector rotating. Color: #FFFF00. Label: 'Rotation'.
Flash all vectors simultaneously for final impact. Color: #00FFFF. Label: 'System'.
